messages:
sofia: Heads-up: we saw an ~8-12% perf regression on recent quantized runs (INT8/FP8) vs last week's baseline for seq_len=512. We need a concise runbook for quantized evaluations so comparisons are reproducible and fair. Starting thread to capture checklist.

james: +1. First big item: warmup policy. My proposal: explicit kernel warmup + KV warmup + steady-state measured tokens. Example: kernel_warmup=50, kv_warmup=50, measure_tokens=10k. Also include a GPU power stabilization window (e.g., 30s) when power-limited.

rajiv: 50/50 is reasonable for quick checks, but for official runs use 300 tokens warmup + 10k measured tokens for throughput numbers. Quantized kernels (esp FP8) can have JIT-like behavior where first few iterations are slower. Let's make phases explicit: 1) environment priming, 2) kernel/loader warmup, 3) KV steady-state.

maria: Add hardware env requirements to the run metadata: GPU model, driver, CUDA, cuDNN, nvidia-smi output, power_limit, fan gov. Document whether MPS was enabled/disabled and any background processes. Differences in power/thermal state will skew results a lot.

sofia: Also require toggles for dynamic batching and scheduler interference. For per-request p50/p95 latency we must disable dynamic batching; for throughput runs enable a documented batching policy.

james: Example run command we can standardize on (feel free to reuse in scripts):
```
./run_infer.sh --model llama-2-70b --precision int8 --batch 1 --seq 512 \n  --warmup-tokens 300 --measure-tokens 10000 --power-limit 250 \n  --kv-cache on --seed 42 --disable-dyn-batching \n  --dump-kernel-map /tmp/kernel_map.json
```

rajiv: Tokenization parity note: always use the same tokenizer binary + vocab file between runs. Tokenizer variance can change token counts and segmentation which affects perf. Record tokenizer hash in metadata.

maria: Calibration guidance for FP8/INT8: share the exact calibration corpus and random seed. Recommended: 2k-5k representative samples (not too small). Log per-layer calibration histograms and store them as artifacts. Avoid reusing calibration samples that match eval/test set.

perf-bot: profile: nvprof trace saved to s3://redwood-perf/1790456789/nvprof.tar.gz -- flamegraph: s3://redwood-perf/1790456789/flame.svg

sofia: KV cache behavior: measure 2 scenarios in every official run: (A) cold-start (no KV cache, single long prompt) and (B) cache-hot (many incremental tokens appended to same session). Report both throughput and p50/p95 latencies for each.

james: Kernel selection telemetry: runtime should emit kernel_map (layer -> kernel_id) and fallback reasons. For comparisons include kernel_map_hash in CSV so we know whether quant kernels were actually chosen. Use --force-kernel to test specific kernels.

rajiv: Fairness checklist between quantized and fp16 baselines: compile with identical compiler flags and thread counts. If quantization changes memory layout, capture the compilation logs and heap usage. When possible run fp16 with the same code path except quant kernel hooks disabled.

maria: Quality checks: alongside perf metrics collect a small evaluation suite (100-500 prompts) and report perplexity / exact match / QA F1. Calibration often trades quality for perf; we need a delta table: (fp16 baseline vs quantized) -> (throughput delta, p95 delta, quality delta).

sofia: Reporting CSV schema (required columns): run_id, commit, model, precision, kernel_map_hash, warmup_tokens, measured_tokens, power_limit, batch, seq_len, throughput_tok_s, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, kv_mode, calib_samples, calib_seed, eval_perplexity, notes, s3_artifacts

james: Also capture low-level counters: sm_efficiency, achieved_occupancy, dram_bw, l2_bandwidth. Attach perf counters as artifacts so we can triage whether regression is compute- or memory-bound.

rajiv: Regression triage flow: 1) reproduce on same commit/env 2) toggle kernel (force quant vs fallback) 3) swap calibration tables 4) bisect commits if kernel change suspected. Keep each run as a discrete run_id and tie to artifacts.

maria: Small practical guidelines: - disable other users on the machine, - pin CPU governor to performance, - set CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to a single GPU, - ensure thermals are pre-warmed with a short burn-in.

sofia: I'll draft the runbook and a small wrapper that executes the three phases, uploads artifacts, and emits the CSV row automatically. Assigning follow-ups: @james for kernel flag testing, @rajiv for calibration params, @maria for infra checklist.

deploy-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf/pull/482 :thumbsup:

sofia: Thanks all — once PR lands we'll start a 48-hour canonical run and compare to last stable baseline. If anyone has additional checks to add, drop them here.
